claim: 87 gustatory projections were reconstructed from the proboscis labellum in the right hemisphere of the adult Drosophila melanogaster brain.
source: We reconstructed 87 gustatory projections from the proboscis labellum in the right hemisphere and 57 from the left, representing the majority of labellar gustatory axons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by the reconstruction work described in the Results section.

claim: 57 gustatory projections were reconstructed from the proboscis labellum in the left hemisphere of the adult Drosophila melanogaster brain.
source: We reconstructed 87 gustatory projections from the proboscis labellum in the right hemisphere and 57 from the left, representing the majority of labellar gustatory axons.
evidence: This is stated directly in the abstract and supported by the reconstruction work described in the Results section.

claim: The reconstructed gustatory projections represent the majority of labellar gustatory axons.
source: We reconstructed 87 gustatory projections from the proboscis labellum in the right hemisphere and 57 from the left, representing the majority of labellar gustatory axons.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and quantified in the Results section where it is estimated that 83-96% of right hemisphere and 54-63% of left hemisphere GRNs were identified.

claim: Gustatory neurons contain a nearly equal number of interspersed pre- and postsynaptic sites.
source: Gustatory neurons contain a nearly equal number of interspersed pre- and postsynaptic sites, with extensive synaptic connectivity among gustatory axons.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and quantified in the Results section where it is reported that on average, a GRN contains 175 (±6 SE) presynaptic sites and 168 (±6 SE) postsynaptic sites.

claim: There is extensive synaptic connectivity among gustatory axons.
source: Gustatory neurons contain a nearly equal number of interspersed pre- and postsynaptic sites, with extensive synaptic connectivity among gustatory axons.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by data showing that GRNs are both pre- and postsynaptic to other GRNs, with each GRN receiving between 2% and 66% (average = 39%) of its synaptic input from other GRNs.

claim: Morphology- and connectivity-based clustering revealed six distinct groups of gustatory neurons in the right hemisphere.
source: Morphology- and connectivity-based clustering revealed six distinct groups, likely representing neurons recognizing different taste modalities.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and demonstrated in Figure 2 with hierarchical clustering analysis.

claim: The six distinct groups identified by clustering likely represent neurons recognizing different taste modalities.
source: Morphology- and connectivity-based clustering revealed six distinct groups, likely representing neurons recognizing different taste modalities.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and supported by NBLAST comparisons with known GRN classes in Figure 3.

claim: The vast majority of synaptic connections are between neurons of the same group.
source: The vast majority of synaptic connections are between neurons of the same group.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract and quantified in the Results section where it is shown that 79% of synapses are between neurons of the same group.

claim: On average, a GRN contains 175 (±6 SE) presynaptic sites.
source: On average, a GRN contains 175 (±6 SE) presynaptic sites and 168 (±6 SE) postsynaptic sites, with individual GRNs showing wide variation in pre- and postsynapse number (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative measurement from the EM reconstruction data.

claim: On average, a GRN contains 168 (±6 SE) postsynaptic sites.
source: On average, a GRN contains 175 (±6 SE) presynaptic sites and 168 (±6 SE) postsynaptic sites, with individual GRNs showing wide variation in pre- and postsynapse number (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative measurement from the EM reconstruction data.

claim: Each GRN receives between 2% and 66% (average = 39%) of its synaptic input from other GRNs.
source: GRNs are both pre- and postsynaptic to other GRNs, with each GRN receiving between 2% and 66% (average = 39%) of its synaptic input from other GRNs (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative measurement from the connectivity analysis.

claim: The reconstructed GRNs represent between 83–96% of the total expected GRNs in the right hemisphere.
source: In total, we identified 87 axonal projections in the right hemisphere. Tracing from the left labial nerve and neural tract in the left hemisphere, we identified 57 additional projections. Misalignments in the EM volume precluded identification of additional GRNs in the left hemisphere. Because there are 90–104 GRNs per labellum (Jaeger et al., 2018; Stocker, 1994), we estimate that we have identified 83–96% of the GRN fibers from the right labellum and 54–63% from the left.
evidence: This is calculated based on the number of reconstructed GRNs (87) compared to the total expected number (90-104) from previous studies.

claim: The reconstructed GRNs represent between 54–63% of the total expected GRNs in the left hemisphere.
source: In total, we identified 87 axonal projections in the right hemisphere. Tracing from the left labial nerve and neural tract in the left hemisphere, we identified 57 additional projections. Misalignments in the EM volume precluded identification of additional GRNs in the left hemisphere. Because there are 90–104 GRNs per labellum (Jaeger et al., 2018; Stocker, 1994), we estimate that we have identified 83–96% of the GRN fibers from the right labellum and 54–63% from the left.
evidence: This is calculated based on the number of reconstructed GRNs (57) compared to the total expected number (90-104) from previous studies.

claim: There are 90–104 GRNs per labellum in Drosophila.
source: Because there are 90–104 GRNs per labellum (Jaeger et al., 2018; Stocker, 1994), we estimate that we have identified 83–96% of the GRN fibers from the right labellum and 54–63% from the left.
evidence: This is cited from previous studies by Jaeger et al., 2018 and Stocker, 1994.

claim: Misalignments in the EM volume precluded identification of additional GRNs in the left hemisphere.
source: Tracing from the left labial nerve and neural tract in the left hemisphere, we identified 57 additional projections. Misalignments in the EM volume precluded identification of additional GRNs in the left hemisphere.
evidence: This is stated as a technical limitation of the dataset.

claim: 79% of GRN-GRN synapses are between neurons of the same group.
source: This analysis revealed that most synapses are between neurons of the same group (79%), while only 21% of the synapses are between GRNs of different groups (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative measurement from the connectivity analysis.

claim: 21% of GRN-GRN synapses are between GRNs of different groups.
source: This analysis revealed that most synapses are between neurons of the same group (79%), while only 21% of the synapses are between GRNs of different groups (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a direct quantitative measurement from the connectivity analysis.

claim: When considering only connections of five or more synapses between GRN pairs, between-group connections represent only 10% of all GRN connections.
source: Focusing on connections of five or more synapses between GRN pairs, representing high-confidence connections (Buhmann et al., 2021; Li et al., 2020; Takemura et al., 2013; Takemura et al., 2015), resulted in the elimination of some but not all between-group connections (Figure 4C), with between-group connections representing only 10% of all GRN connections.
evidence: This is a direct quantitative measurement from the connectivity analysis using a threshold of 5 or more synapses.

claim: Drosophila melanogaster has five different classes of gustatory receptor neurons (GRNs) in adults that detect different taste modalities.
source: Molecular genetic approaches coupled with physiology and behavior have established five different classes of gustatory receptor neurons (GRNs) in adult Drosophila that detect different taste modalities.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: One class of GRNs expresses members of the gustatory receptor (GR) family, including Gr5a and Gr64f, detects sugars and elicits acceptance behavior.
source: One class, expressing members of the gustatory receptor (GR) family, including Gr5a and Gr64f, detects sugars and elicits acceptance behavior (Dahanukar et al., 2001; Dahanukar et al., 2007; Thorne et al., 2004; Wang et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: A second class of GRNs expresses different GRs, including Gr66a, detects bitter compounds and mediates rejection behavior.
source: A second class expressing different GRs, including Gr66a, detects bitter compounds and mediates rejection behavior (Thorne et al., 2004; Wang et al., 2004; Weiss et al., 2011).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: A third class of GRNs contains the ion channel Ppk28 and detects water.
source: A third class contains the ion channel Ppk28 and detects water (Cameron et al., 2010; Chen et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The fourth class of GRNs expresses the Ir94e ionotropic receptor.
source: The fourth expresses the Ir94e ionotropic receptor, whereas the fifth contains the Ppk23 ion channel (Jaeger et al., 2018; Thistle et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations.

claim: The fifth class of GRNs contains the Ppk23 ion channel.
source: The fourth expresses the Ir94e ionotropic receptor, whereas the fifth contains the Ppk23 ion channel (Jaeger et al., 2018; Thistle et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Ir94e-expressing GRNs have been proposed to mediate detection of low-salt concentrations.
source: These cells have been proposed to mediate detection of low-salt and high-salt concentrations, respectively (Jaeger et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Ppk23-expressing GRNs have been proposed to mediate detection of high-salt concentrations.
source: These cells have been proposed to mediate detection of low-salt and high-salt concentrations, respectively (Jaeger et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by a citation.

claim: Gustatory neurons from each labellum half send bilaterally symmetric axonal projections to the subesophageal zone (SEZ) of the fly brain via the labial nerves.
source: Gustatory neurons from each labellum half send bilaterally symmetric axonal projections to the subesophageal zone (SEZ) of the fly brain via the labial nerves.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by citations.

claim: Gustatory axons terminate in the medial SEZ in a region called the anterior central sensory center (ACSC).
source: Gustatory axons terminate in the medial SEZ in a region called the anterior central sensory center (ACSC) (Hartenstein et al., 2018; Miyazaki and Ito, 2010; Thorne et al., 2004; Wang et al., 2004).
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Axons from bitter gustatory neurons send branches to the midline and form an interconnected medial ring.
source: Axons from bitter gustatory neurons send branches to the midline and form an interconnected medial ring, whereas other gustatory axons remain ipsilateral and anterolateral to bitter projections.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by the anatomical observations in the Results section.

claim: Non-bitter gustatory axons remain ipsilateral and anterolateral to bitter projections.
source: Axons from bitter gustatory neurons send branches to the midline and form an interconnected medial ring, whereas other gustatory axons remain ipsilateral and anterolateral to bitter projections.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by the anatomical observations in the Results section.

claim: Synapses are sparse along the main neuronal tract and abundant at the terminal arborizations of GRNs.
source: Synapses are sparse along the main neuronal tract and abundant at the terminal arborizations (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Each GRN has a large number of pre- and postsynaptic sites intermixed along the arbors.
source: Each GRN has a large number of pre- and postsynaptic sites intermixed along the arbors (Figure 1E and G–I), characteristic of fly neurites (Bates et al., 2020a; Meinertzhagen, 2018; Olsen and Wilson, 2008; Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1E and G-I.

claim: The intermixing of pre- and postsynaptic sites along arbors is characteristic of fly neurites.
source: Each GRN has a large number of pre- and postsynaptic sites intermixed along the arbors (Figure 1E and G–I), characteristic of fly neurites (Bates et al., 2020a; Meinertzhagen, 2018; Olsen and Wilson, 2008; Takemura et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The reconstructed neurites overlap with the known projection pattern of sugar and bitter GRNs in the registered fly brain template.
source: We confirmed that the reconstructed neurites overlap with the known projection pattern of sugar and bitter GRNs in the registered fly brain template (Figure 1—figure supplement 1; Bogovic et al., 2020), demonstrating that we have identified and traced GRNs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1.

claim: The presence of T-shaped structures characteristic of presynaptic release sites ('T bars'), synaptic vesicles, and a synaptic cleft was used to identify a synapse.
source: The presence of T-shaped structures characteristic of presynaptic release sites ('T bars'), synaptic vesicles, and a synaptic cleft was used to identify a synapse, consistent with previous studies (Zheng et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation.

claim: Hierarchical clustering of GRN axons was performed using Ward's method.
source: We then used Ward's method to hierarchically cluster GRNs into groups (Ward 1963).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Six groups was chosen as the number that minimizes within-cluster variance for the right hemisphere GRNs.
source: We chose six groups as the number that minimizes within-cluster variance (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A; Braun et al., 2010).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Each group in the right hemisphere is composed of 7–23 GRNs that occupy discrete zones in the SEZ and share anatomically similar terminal branches.
source: Each group is composed of 7–23 GRNs that occupy discrete zones in the SEZ and share anatomically similar terminal branches (Figure 2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 2.

claim: Groups 1 and 2 best match bitter projections.
source: Groups 1 and 2 best match bitter projections, forming a characteristic medial ringed web (Figure 3A and B).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3A and B.

claim: Group 3 projections show greatest similarity to low-salt GRNs, with distinctive dorsolateral branches.
source: Group 3 projections show greatest similarity to low-salt GRNs, with distinctive dorsolateral branches (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3C.

claim: Groups 4 and 5 best match sugar GRNs.
source: Groups 4 and 5 best match sugar GRNs (Figure 3D and E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3D and E.

claim: Group 4 is hypothesized to be composed of sugar GRNs because it contains a dorsolateral branch seen in Gr64f projections.
source: Because group 4 contains a dorsolateral branch seen in Gr64f projections and not seen in group 5 projections, we hypothesize that group 4 is composed of sugar GRNs and that the remaining group 5 is composed of high-salt GRNs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a hypothesis based on anatomical features.

claim: Group 5 is hypothesized to be composed of high-salt GRNs.
source: Because group 4 contains a dorsolateral branch seen in Gr64f projections and not seen in group 5 projections, we hypothesize that group 4 is composed of sugar GRNs and that the remaining group 5 is composed of high-salt GRNs.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a hypothesis based on anatomical features.

claim: Group 6 best matches water GRNs.
source: Group 6 best matches water GRNs (Figure 3F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3F.

claim: Clustering analysis of GRNs from the left hemisphere yielded seven groups of 4–15 neurons.
source: An identical clustering analysis of GRNs from the left hemisphere yielded seven groups of 4–15 neurons (Figure 3—figure supplements 1–2).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 3—figure supplements 1–2.

claim: In the left hemisphere, groups 1 and 2 best match bitter projections.
source: Groups 1 and 2 best match bitter projections and group 6 best matches low-salt projections (see section 'NBLAST analysis for taste modality assignment'), with anatomy consistent with known projection patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: In the left hemisphere, group 6 best matches low-salt projections.
source: Groups 1 and 2 best match bitter projections and group 6 best matches low-salt projections (see section 'NBLAST analysis for taste modality assignment'), with anatomy consistent with known projection patterns.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Other groups in the left hemisphere are not well-resolved.
source: Other groups are not well-resolved (see section 'NBLAST analysis for taste modality assignment'), arguing that a more complete dataset is necessary to resolve GRN categories in the left hemisphere.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section.

claim: Group 4 neurons receive 1468 synapses from other group 4 neurons.
source: For example, group 4 neurons receive 1468 synapses from other group 4 neurons and 38 from group 3, 156 from group 5, and 130 from group 6 neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a specific example of connectivity.

claim: Group 4 neurons receive 38 synapses from group 3 neurons.
source: For example, group 4 neurons receive 1468 synapses from other group 4 neurons and 38 from group 3, 156 from group 5, and 130 from group 6 neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a specific example of connectivity.

claim: Group 4 neurons receive 156 synapses from group 5 neurons.
source: For example, group 4 neurons receive 1468 synapses from other group 4 neurons and 38 from group 3, 156 from group 5, and 130 from group 6 neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a specific example of connectivity.

claim: Group 4 neurons receive 130 synapses from group 6 neurons.
source: For example, group 4 neurons receive 1468 synapses from other group 4 neurons and 38 from group 3, 156 from group 5, and 130 from group 6 neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a specific example of connectivity.

claim: Activation of sugar GRNs did not activate bitter cells.
source: Activation of sugar or water GRNs did not activate bitter cells, nor did bitter cell activation elicit responses in sugar or water axons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 2E and F, Figure 5—figure supplement 3G and H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Activation of water GRNs did not activate bitter cells.
source: Activation of sugar or water GRNs did not activate bitter cells, nor did bitter cell activation elicit responses in sugar or water axons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 2E and F, Figure 5—figure supplement 3G and H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Bitter cell activation did not elicit responses in sugar axons.
source: Activation of sugar or water GRNs did not activate bitter cells, nor did bitter cell activation elicit responses in sugar or water axons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 2E and F, Figure 5—figure supplement 3G and H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in the referenced figures.

claim: Bitter cell activation did not elicit responses in water axons.
source: Activation of sugar or water GRNs did not activate bitter cells, nor did bitter cell activation elicit responses in sugar or water axons (Figure 5—figure supplement 1E–H, Figure 5—figure supplement 2E and F, Figure 5—figure supplement 3G and H).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in the referenced figures.

claim: No responses were observed in sugar GRNs upon water GRN activation.
source: Similarly, we did not observe responses in sugar GRNs upon water GRN activation (Figure 5C and D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J) or responses in water GRNs upon sugar GRN activation (Figure 5I and J, Figure 5—figure supplement 3E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in the referenced figures.

claim: No responses were observed in water GRNs upon sugar GRN activation.
source: Similarly, we did not observe responses in sugar GRNs upon water GRN activation (Figure 5C and D, Figure 5—figure supplement 2I and J) or responses in water GRNs upon sugar GRN activation (Figure 5I and J, Figure 5—figure supplement 3E and F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in the referenced figures.

claim: No change in voltage was observed in sugar GRNs upon activation of water GRNs.
source: To examine whether inhibitory interactions might exist between two GRN classes, we expressed the voltage indicator ArcLight (Cao et al., 2013), which reliably reports hyperpolarization, in sugar GRNs while activating water GRNs via P2X2 and vice versa. These experiments revealed no change in voltage in one appetitive gustatory class upon activation of the other (Figure 5E–F and K–L, Figure 5—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in the referenced figures.

claim: No change in voltage was observed in water GRNs upon activation of sugar GRNs.
source: To examine whether inhibitory interactions might exist between two GRN classes, we expressed the voltage indicator ArcLight (Cao et al., 2013), which reliably reports hyperpolarization, in sugar GRNs while activating water GRNs via P2X2 and vice versa. These experiments revealed no change in voltage in one appetitive gustatory class upon activation of the other (Figure 5E–F and K–L, Figure 5—figure supplement 7).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in the referenced figures.

claim: No communication between appetitive GRNs was observed by calcium or voltage imaging of gustatory axons.
source: Overall, despite the potential for crosstalk between different modalities revealed by EM, we observed no communication between appetitive GRNs by calcium or voltage imaging of gustatory axons.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a summary of the imaging experiments.

claim: In the adult olfactory system, approximately 40% of the input onto olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) comes from other ORNs projecting to the same olfactory glomerulus.
source: In the adult olfactory system, approximately 40% of the input onto olfactory receptor neurons (ORNs) comes from other ORNs projecting to the same olfactory glomerulus (Horne et al., 2018; Schlegel et al., 2021; Tobin et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Mechanosensory projections from Johnston's organ of the same submodality are anatomically segregated and synaptically connected.
source: Similarly, mechanosensory projections from Johnston's organ of the same submodality are anatomically segregated and synaptically connected (Hampel et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: In Drosophila larvae, 25% of gustatory neuron inputs are from other GRNs.
source: In Drosophila larvae, 25% of gustatory neuron inputs are from other GRNs, although functional classes were not resolved (Miroschnikow et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: A general function of sensory–sensory connections seen across sensory modalities may be to enhance weak signals or increase dynamic range.
source: A general function of sensory–sensory connections seen across sensory modalities may be to enhance weak signals or increase dynamic range.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a hypothesis based on observations across multiple sensory systems.

claim: Bitter projections cluster into two distinct groups, which may be comprised of bitter GRNs from different taste bristle classes or bitter GRNs with different response properties.
source: Interestingly, in our clustering analysis, we find that bitter projections cluster into two distinct groups. We hypothesize that these different subsets are comprised of bitter GRNs from different taste bristle classes or bitter GRNs with different response properties (Dweck and Carlson, 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a hypothesis based on the clustering results.

claim: The labial nerve is a compound nerve, carrying sensory axons from the labellum, maxillary palp, and eye, as well as motor axons innervating proboscis musculature.
source: The labial nerve is a compound nerve, carrying sensory axons from the labellum, maxillary palp, and eye, as well as motor axons innervating proboscis musculature (Hampel et al., 2017; Hartenstein et al., 2018; Miyazaki and Ito, 2010; Nayak and Singh, 1983; Rajashekhar and Singh, 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by multiple citations.

claim: Different sensory afferents occupy different domains in the SEZ, with labellar gustatory axons terminating in the ACSC.
source: Different sensory afferents occupy different domains in the SEZ, with labellar gustatory axons terminating in the ACSC (Hartenstein et al., 2018; Miyazaki and Ito, 2010; Thorne et al., 2004; Wang et al., 2004; Figure 1A).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by multiple citations.

claim: The arborization pattern of reconstructed GRNs recapitulates the labellar sensory projections of the ACSC.
source: This arborization pattern recapitulates the labellar sensory projections of the ACSC (Hartenstein et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and supported by a citation.

claim: Neurotransmitter predictions of GRNs, in general, do not predict a clear majority neurotransmitter.
source: Neurotransmitter predictions of GRNs, in general, do not predict a clear majority neurotransmitter (Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2; Eckstein et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 4—figure supplements 1 and 2.

claim: GRNs may release multiple neurotransmitters or neurotransmitter predictions should be considered uncertain until further testing.
source: This suggests that GRNs may release multiple neurotransmitters or that neurotransmitter predictions should be considered uncertain until further testing (Eckstein et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as an interpretation of the neurotransmitter prediction results.

claim: The projections from the left and right labial nerves are symmetric and converge in a dense web in the anterior central SEZ.
source: The projections from the left and right labial nerves are symmetric and converge in a dense web in the anterior central SEZ (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Neurites with small- to medium-sized diameters in the dorsomedial labial nerve projected along a single neural tract to the anterior central region of the SEZ.
source: In tracing axons, we found that neurites with small- to medium-sized diameters in the dorsomedial labial nerve (Figure 1C) projected along a single neural tract (Figure 1D) to the anterior central region of the SEZ.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figures 1C and 1D.

claim: Individual GRN fibers followed along the same tract and showed variation in terminal branching.
source: Individual fibers followed along the same tract and showed variation in terminal branching (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is stated in the Results section and shown in Figure 1E.

claim: Skeletons were traced to completion either entirely manually or using a combination of an automated segmentation and manual tracing.
source: Skeletons were traced to completion either entirely manually or using a combination of an automated segmentation (Li et al., 2019) and manual tracing as previously described (Hampel et al., 2020).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: Skeletons were reviewed by a second specialist, so that the final reconstruction presents the consensus assessment of at least two specialists.
source: Skeletons were reviewed by a second specialist, so that the final reconstruction presents the consensus assessment of at least two specialists.
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: FAFB neuronal reconstructions will be available from Virtual Fly Brain.
source: FAFB neuronal reconstructions will be available from Virtual Fly Brain (https://fafb.catmaid.virtualflybrain.org/).
evidence: This is stated in the Materials and methods section.

claim: The large numbers of chemical synapses between GRNs within a group may provide a mechanism to amplify signals of the same taste modality.
source: The large numbers of chemical synapses between GRNs within a group may provide a mechanism to amplify signals of the same taste modality.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a hypothesis based on the connectivity data.

claim: Weak connectivity between GRNs of different groups may serve to integrate taste information from different modalities before transmission to downstream circuitry.
source: In contrast, weak connectivity between GRNs of different groups may serve to integrate taste information from different modalities before transmission to downstream circuitry.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a hypothesis based on the connectivity data.

claim: Misclassification of individual GRNs in the clustering analysis may result in over- or underestimates of GRN connectivity within and between groups.
source: We note that misclassification of individual GRNs in the clustering analysis may result in over- or underestimates of GRN connectivity within and between groups.
evidence: This is stated in the Results section as a caveat to the connectivity analysis.

claim: Interactions between GRN modalities may be dependent on a feeding state or act on a time frame not examined in this study.
source: It is possible that these interactions are dependent on a feeding state or act on a time frame not examined in this study.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a possible explanation for the lack of observed interactions.

claim: Activation between GRN modalities may fall below the detection threshold of calcium or voltage imaging.
source: Alternatively, activation may fall below the detection threshold of calcium or voltage imaging.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a possible explanation for the lack of observed interactions.

claim: The few synapses between different GRN groups may not be relevant for taste processing.
source: Additionally, far fewer synapses occur between anatomical classes than within classes, especially restricting analyses to neurons connected by five or more synapses (Figure 4C), suggesting that the few synapses may not be relevant for taste processing.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a possible explanation for the lack of observed interactions.

claim: The anatomy and connectivity-based clustering may not categorize all individual GRNs correctly, and misclassification of GRNs would impact connectivity analyses.
source: Finally, the anatomy and connectivity-based clustering may not categorize all individual GRNs correctly, and misclassification of GRNs would impact connectivity analyses.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a caveat to the connectivity analysis.

claim: Presynaptic connectivity between different GRN classes does not substantially contribute to taste processing.
source: Regardless, our studies suggest that presynaptic connectivity between different GRN classes does not substantially contribute to taste processing.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion based on the imaging experiments.

claim: This study resolves the majority of labellar gustatory projections and their synaptic connections.
source: Overall, this study resolves the majority of labellar gustatory projections and their synaptic connections, revealing that gustatory projections are segregated based on taste modality and sensory–sensory connectivity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the study's findings.

claim: Gustatory projections are segregated based on taste modality and sensory–sensory connectivity.
source: Overall, this study resolves the majority of labellar gustatory projections and their synaptic connections, revealing that gustatory projections are segregated based on taste modality and sensory–sensory connectivity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a summary of the study's findings.

claim: The identification of GRNs detecting different taste modalities provides an inroad to enable the examination of the downstream circuits that integrate taste information and guide feeding decisions.
source: The identification of GRNs detecting different taste modalities now provides an inroad to enable the examination of the downstream circuits that integrate taste information and guide feeding decisions.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a conclusion about the implications of the study.

claim: GRN categories may be further refined upon reconstruction of the entire GRN population or upon analysis that includes postsynaptic partners.
source: GRN categories may be further refined upon reconstruction of the entire GRN population or upon analysis that includes postsynaptic partners.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a suggestion for future work.

claim: GRNs are found at different locations on the proboscis labellum and are housed in three taste bristle types.
source: In addition, GRNs are found at different locations on the proboscis labellum and are housed in three taste bristle types (Stocker, 1994).
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by a citation.

claim: Segregation based on labellar location or bristle type may further divide the GRN categories described in this study.
source: Segregation based on labellar location or bristle type may further divide the GRN categories described here.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a hypothesis.

claim: An emerging theme from EM reconstructions of Drosophila sensory systems is that sensory neurons of the same subclass are synaptically connected.
source: An emerging theme stemming from EM reconstructions of Drosophila sensory systems is that sensory neurons of the same subclass are synaptically connected.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion and supported by examples from multiple sensory systems.

claim: Different sensory neuron subclasses have spatially segregated axonal termini in the brain, thereby constraining the potential for connectivity.
source: In general, different sensory neuron subclasses have spatially segregated axonal termini in the brain, thereby constraining the potential for connectivity.
evidence: This is stated in the Discussion as a general observation about sensory systems.

claim: The Drosophila melanogaster gustatory system is an attractive model to examine the synaptic transmission of gustatory neurons.
source: The Drosophila melanogaster gustatory system is an attractive model to examine the synaptic transmission of gustatory neurons.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction as a rationale for the study.

claim: The peripheral strategy for taste detection in Drosophila is akin to mammals.
source: In addition to well-characterized gustatory neurons and a peripheral strategy for taste detection akin to mammals (Yarmolinsky et al., 2009), the reduced number of neurons in the Drosophila nervous system and the availability of electron microscopy (EM) brain volumes offer the opportunity to examine gustatory transmission with high resolution.
evidence: This is stated in the Introduction and supported by a citation.
